chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Aban, from Abdul Malik who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Fast of Tasua and Ashura from the month of Muharram, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Tasua is a day in which Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and his companions, may Allah be pleased with them, were surrounded in Karbala, and the cavalry of the people of Syria gathered against him and encamped upon him, and Ibn Marjana and Umar ibn Sa'd rejoiced at the abundance and multitude of the cavalry, and they considered Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and his companions, may Allah be pleased with them, to be weak, and they were convinced that no helper would come to Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) nor would the people of Iraq support him, by my father, the oppressed, the alienated.'

Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'And as for the day of Ashura, it is a day in which Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was killed as a corpse among his companions, and his companions were corpses around him, stripped. So, can a Fast be on that day? No! By the Lord of the Sacred House, it is not a day of Fasting, and it is not except a day of grief and calamity that entered upon the inhabitants of the sky and the inhabitants of the earth and all the believers.'

And it is a day of joy and happiness for Ibn Marjana and the progeny of Ziyad and the people of Syria. May Allah be Wrathful upon them and upon their offspring. And that is a day in which all the spots of the earth wept for him, except for the spot of Syria. So whoever fasts it or considers it fortunate, Allah will resurrect him with the progeny of Ziyad, morphed of the heart, Angered upon; and whoever hoards provisions in his house, Allah the Exalted will cause hypocrisy to be the end result in his heart until the day he meets Him, and He will snatch away the Blessing from him and from the people of his household and his children, and the Satan will be his partner in all of that.'

key_terms.ابْنُ مَرْجَانَةَ: Umar ibn Hubayra, known as Ibn Marjana, a Umayyad commander
key_terms.عُمَرُ بْنُ سَعْدٍ: Umar ibn Sa'd, the commander of the army at Karbala
key_terms.كَرْبَلَاءَ: Karbala, the site of the martyrdom of Imam Husayn
key_terms.مَمْسُوخُ الْقَلْبِ: Morphed of the heart, indicating a change in nature or state

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fasting on the 9th and 10th of Muharram according to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between Tasua, marked by the encirclement of Imam Husayn (AS), and Ashura, the day of his martyrdom, declaring the latter a day of profound grief rather than fasting. He provides a theological rationale for the Shia practice of fasting on Ashura by contrasting the mourning of the faithful with the joy of the Umayyad enemies, specifically Ibn Marjana and the people of Sham. The Imam warns that those who fast or celebrate this day share the spiritual fate of the Umayyads, suffering from hypocrisy and the removal of divine blessing.

en.hubeali: And from him, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Aban, from Abdul Malik who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the Fast of ‘Tasua’ (9<sup>th</sup> Muharram), and Ashura (10<sup>th</sup> Muharram) from the month of Muharram. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Tasua is a day in which Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> and his<sup>asws</sup> companions, may Allah<sup>azwj</sup> be Pleased with them, were surrounded in Kerbala, and the cavalries of the people of Syria were gathered against him<sup>asws</sup>, and inflicted injuries upon him<sup>asws</sup>; and Ibn Marjana and Umar Bin Sa’ad were joyful due to the large numbers of the cavalries and its abundance, and Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> and his<sup>asws</sup> companions, may Allah<sup>azwj</sup> be Pleased with them, were weakened during it, and they were convinced that no helper would be coming to Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> nor would the people of Al-Iraq support him<sup>asws</sup>. By my<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup>, the oppressed, the alienated.

Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And as for the day of Ashura, so it is a day in which Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> was injured to bits between his<sup>asws</sup> companions, and his<sup>asws</sup> companions were injured to bits around him<sup>asws</sup>, stripped. So, can a Fast happen to be during that day? Never! By the Lord<sup>azwj</sup> of the Sacred House, it is not a day of Fasting, and it is not except for a day of grief, and the difficulties enter upon the inhabitants of the sky and the inhabitants of the earth, and the entirety of the Believers.

And, it is a day of happiness and joy for Ibn Marjana and the progeny of Ziyad, and the people of Syria. May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> be Wrathful upon them and upon their offspring. And, that is a day in which the entirety of the spots of the earth wailed upon him<sup>asws</sup> except for the spot of Syria. So the one who Fasts, or (believes to be) fortunate by it, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Resurrect him with the progeny of Ziyad, morphed of the heart, Angered upon; and the one who hoards provisions in his house, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the Exalted would Cause his end result for hypocrisy to be in his heart up to the day he meets Him<sup>azwj</sup>, and Snatch away the Blessings from him, and from the people of his household, and his children, and the Satan<sup>la</sup> would be his participant in the entirety of that’.
en.sarwar: 7. It is narrated from him (narrator of previous Hadith) from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Aban from ‘Abd al-Malik who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the fast on the day of ‘Ashura’ of the month of Muharram. He (the Imam) said, ‘Tasu‘a’ (ninth of Muharram) was the day when they had surrounded al-Husayn, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and his friends, may Allah be pleased with them, in Karbala’. The horsemen of al-Sham had come together against him, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and had taken him under siege. Ibn Marjanah and ‘Umar ibn Sa‘d were happy because of the huge number of horsemen on their side, and they made al-Husayn, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and his friends, may Allah be pleased with them, very weak. They became certain that no one will come to help al-Husayn, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and people of Iraq will not support him. I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for the cause of my great-grandfather who had very few supporters.’

He (the Imam) then said, ‘The day of ‘Ashura’ is the day on which al-Husayn, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, was murdered and his friends around him were all murdered and looted. How can there be fast on that day! No, by the Lord of the sacred house there is no fasting on such a day. It is only a day of mourning and lamentation that came upon the inhabitants of the sky and earth and all believing people.

It is a day of happiness and joy for ibn Marjanah and family of Ziyad and people of al-Sham, may Allah subject them to His anger as well as their offspring. This was a day when all locations of earth wept except al-Sham. Those who fast on this day or take it for blessing will be raised, by Allah, with the family of Ziyad with their hearts metamorphosed and subjected to anger. Whoever seeks any saving for their homes on this day will be made by Allah as a seed of hypocrisy in his heart up to the Day of Judgment, blessing is removed thereof, from his family, and children. Satan will share him in all of such savings.’”
